source_quote: Projected MOIC (5gmal.comDEAL SNAPSHOТ Issuer The American Housing Corporation Ownership 1.75% Round Series A Instrument Series A Preferred (Priced) Allocation Co-Invest: $5,000,000 Valuation Cap $235,000,000 (pre-money) THE OPPORTUNITY Residential construction has not meaningfully benefited from industrial-scale productivity improvements, despite a persistent housing shortage and structurally high construction costs. AHC's thesis is that the path to scale is not "modular houses as a product," but a repeatable, software-orchestrated manufacturing + assembly system that can be deployed across geographies with predictable cost, timeline, and quality. AHC's approach is componentized (e.g., bathrooms/kitchens + panels) and built for factory repeatability; each module is designed to fit standard shipping containers for cost-efficient logistics and national deployment. That production line is married with a software layer (Alamo) as the "manufacturing OS." Alamo is intended to manage underwriting, site planning, factory production, and onsite assembly-creating a compounding operational dataset and tighter feedback loops than contractor-led construction. AHC is explicitly structuring the business so real estate capital can fund land + builds (PropCo) while the venture-backed OpCo captures high-margin manufacturing + system IP-aligning the capital stack with the growth bottleneck (production capacity) for efficient scaling. AHC is raising $50M to build out their first "Gigafactory" that will enable AHC to drive costs lower, expand margins, and scale production from dozens of units a year to over a thousand. The Series A round is fully subscribed and led by Contrary Ventures. Our participation in their Seed round and leading their last Bridge round gives our LPs exclusive access to allocation. WHY NOW Manufacturing inflection AHC has moved from concept to validated system quickly, and the binding constraint is now production capacity-not demand. Capital structure advantage The OpCo/PropCo model is designed to scale with real estate capital while preserving venture-style upside in the manufacturing + software layer. Execution velocity The team has shown unusually fast iteration and delivery cadence-de-risking "can they build" and shifting the question to "can they scale."
